subject: Observability kickoff: telemetry owners & incident roles
messages:
From: Elena Roberts <elena@fastretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastretail.com
Date: Sat, 16 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability kickoff: telemetry owners & incident roles

Hi Marcus / Laura —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re ready to kick off the implementation phase for tracing, dashboards, and alert routing. Goal is to have an initial telemetry handoff completed ahead of the pilot by Feb 14.

Quick context from our side:
- Team: FastRetail platform ops (20 people), SRE triage (4 primary on-call)
- Current telemetry: mix of Datadog traces, a small home-built event bus, and CloudWatch for infra.
- Pain points: inconsistent error taxonomy across services; alert fatigue from noisy payment/checkout alerts; missing end-to-end traces for cart abandonment flows.

Can you confirm:
1) Who on Redwood will own the dashboard set and runbook templates?
2) Proposed alert routing for critical payment errors vs. informational infra alerts?
3) A simple owner matrix we can use to approve the initial rollout?

Attached is our current inventory export for your review.

Thanks — happy to take a short call next week if that helps.

— Elena Roberts
Head of Platform Operations, FastRetail
[Attachment: current-telemetry-inventory.csv (CSV)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Roberts <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff: telemetry owners & incident roles

Thanks Elena — this is a great starting point. Short answers first:
- Redwood will own the canonical dashboard set for the pilot (Marcus / Monica).
- We recommend a two-tier alert routing: Pager (on-call SRE) for payment-critical errors + payments SLO breaches; Ops channel (Slack/email) for infra degradations and informational alerts.
- We’ll produce an owner matrix and a runbook template for review by Jan 26.

Planned next steps:
1) Internal alignment (this week) — assign owners and map dashboards to FastRetail services.
2) Delivery of handshake matrix + runbook template (by Jan 26).
3) Short review call with FastRetail to validate mappings and SLOs (Jan 28).

I’ve attached the initial handshake matrix workbook that lays out owner, reviewer, and notification channel per alert category. Monica will drive the dashboard templates; Laura will take the tracing hooks and error taxonomy design. Aditya will coordinate the pilot rollout schedule and on-call mapping.

Suggested meeting: Jan 28, 10:00am PT (30 min) — will that work for you?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: handshake-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Elena Roberts <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff: telemetry owners & incident roles

Thanks Marcus / Elena — adding a few specifics so the team has clear deliverables.

On tracing hooks:
- We’ll instrument the cart -> checkout -> payment path with explicit span names and attributes for user_id, cart_id, payment_gateway, and error_code.
- Proposal: standardized attribute prefix "fr." (fastretail) to avoid collisions (example: fr.payment.gateway).

On error taxonomy:
- Level 1 (critical): payment processing failures, double-charges, data-loss
- Level 2 (major): increased latency impacting conversion > 20%
- Level 3 (minor): transient errors and recoverable client failures

Alert routing (brief):
- Critical (Level 1): PagerDuty -> SRE on-call pager + Ops escalation Slack channel (#fastretail-critical).
- Major (Level 2): Ops Slack channel + duty email (no pager).
- Minor (Level 3): Daily digest to product/infra owners.

Runbook template: I’ve sketched a minimal runbook skeleton that includes: symptoms, immediate mitigation steps, recovery checklist, stakeholder notifications, post-incident notes. Attaching the template for review.

Quote: "On Mon, 18 Jan 2027 at 08:04 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:"
> I’ve attached the initial handshake matrix workbook that lays out owner, reviewer, and notification channel per alert category. Monica will drive the dashboard templates; Laura will take the tracing hooks and error taxonomy design. Aditya will coordinate the pilot rollout schedule and on-call mapping.

Action items I’ll take this week:
- Populate tracing hook examples for two services (cart-service, checkout-service).
- Draft the first pass error taxonomy doc and map to alert severity.

— Laura Bennett
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runbook-template.md (MD)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Roberts <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff: telemetry owners & incident roles

Elena — thanks for the quick turn. Finalizing timeline and asks below.

Confirmed deliverables (dates):
- Jan 22: Handshake matrix (owners + notification channels) — Marcus / Monica (attached).
- Jan 26: Tracing hooks examples + Error taxonomy draft — Laura.
- Jan 28: Review call with FastRetail (30 min) to approve SLOs & alert routing.
- Feb 7: Pilot dashboard deploy to FastRetail staging.

SLO suggestions to consider for the review call (short):
- Payment processing p95 latency < 350ms
- Checkout completion rate >= 98% (rollup daily window)
- Error budget burn alert: > 5% increase in payment error rate over baseline in 1 hour

Attached a CSV that maps alert name -> channel -> primary owner for your team to confirm. If the Jan 28 slot works we’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda: 1) owners and SLOs; 2) tracing hook examples; 3) runbook acknowledgment.

Please confirm meeting availability and any additional stakeholders (security or procurement) that should be looped in.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-alert-routing.csv (CSV)]
